risks.note: Volatility in commodity prices, particularly ferro alloys and aluminium, driven by global and domestic supply-demand dynamics, can materially affect input costs and margins. Mitigated by continuous tracking of commodity trends, agile pricing, product-mix diversification and evaluation of hedging instruments.

Shifts in trade policy, including the withdrawal of protective measures such as safeguard duties or quality control orders, could affect margins and the competitive position of domestic manufacturing. Mitigated by close policy tracking, widening the market footprint to reduce dependence on any single geography or policy regime, and working with industry bodies.

risks.risk: Import-driven competition and pricing distortions in specialised downstream products
risks.note: Global steel prices and low-cost imports weighed on domestic manufacturers and allied industries over the previous two years; even after the 12% safeguard duty on flat steel imports and stricter quality norms, persistent unfair competition and pricing distortions continue to affect parts of the value chain, particularly specialised downstream products, demanding continued discipline from ancillary suppliers such as the Company.

Significant overcapacity in the domestic market kept the segment subdued through the year; the Company consciously refrained from unviable price competition to protect profitability, which constrains volumes until market conditions stabilise and commercial viability improves.

risks.risk: Project management / execution risk in newer businesses
risks.note: Delays or inefficiencies in executing capital projects, including capacity expansions in newer businesses, may cause cost escalation and defer planned growth. Mitigated by structured planning frameworks, detailed feasibility studies and risk analyses before committing capital, and cross-functional issue resolution.

Disruptions from environmental events, geopolitical tensions or concentration among suppliers can affect operational continuity and cost efficiency. Mitigated by alternative sourcing channels, a diversified supplier base, improved supply chain visibility and contingency plans.

Defaults by customers on payment obligations expose the Company to credit risk; significant defaults can strain cash flows and profitability. Mitigated by thorough credit assessment, keeping the customer portfolio broad to avoid overdependence on a few accounts, defined credit terms and close receivables monitoring.

Manufacturing operations demand the highest safety standards; any lapse in safety protocols can disrupt operations, invite legal consequences and damage the Company's reputation. Mitigated by rigorous protocols with continuous training, periodic safety audits and detailed risk assessments across facilities, and a safety-first culture at every level.

themes.title: Refractories & metallurgical consumables
themes.need: Refractory and metallurgical-consumable makers earn recurring per-tonne pricing tied to steel/cement OUTPUT volumes - an annuity-like wear-parts thesis, not the producers own realisation cycle. Q1FY27 turned the graphite-electrode leg on PRICE rather than demand: HEG's standalone EBITDA swung from -INR 126cr in Q4FY26 to +INR 211cr at a 29% margin on LOWER volumes, entirely realisation and mix, after GrafTech announced $600-1,200/t and Tokai $930/t electrode price increases. The timing is unusually favourable - HEG's own price rises only take effect from October because its book is committed through Sept/Oct, while needle-coke inflation (+$200-300/t on 10-15% of electrode cost) hits the P&L only Nov-Jan. RAIN adds the calcined-petroleum-coke anode consumable into aluminium smelters (Carbon EBITDA up INR 1.63B as CPC prices ran $50-100 above the West on China's supply crunch); SMLT the cored-wire leg into steel mills.
themes.driver: Steel/cement output-volume growth driving per-tonne consumables demand; HEG's October price increases landing against needle-coke inflation arriving only Nov-Jan - Q3 is the quarter the margin-maintenance promise is decided.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Flagship company of the Desraj Bansal Group and, by its own account, India's leading manufacturer and exporter of metallurgical consumables such as Cored Wires and Aluminium Flipping Coils, now scaling a welding consumables business and taking a measured entry into biotechnology.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Sarthak Metals manufactures and exports metallurgical consumables - principally Cored Wires and Aluminium Flipping Coils - used to advance and fine-tune steel manufacturing processes, and is the preferred supplier to some of India's largest steel players. Headquartered in Bhilai, Chhattisgarh, it leverages proximity to a major steel production hub and operates ISO 9001 certified facilities with rigorous testing and inspection. Welding consumables, led by Flux Cored Wires, have emerged as the new growth engine, with seven grades across carbon steel, stainless steel and hardfacing at a capacity of 3,600 TPA sold through a dealer-led model, while a pilot Solid State Fermentation R&D facility at Nagpur marks a measured entry into enzyme technologies for the ethanol ecosystem.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India remains one of the most attractive long-term steel markets globally, supported by sustained investment in infrastructure, railways, housing, manufacturing and government-led capital expenditure, with the country targeting 300 million tonnes of steel capacity by 2030
- Policy support strengthened: the 12% safeguard duty introduced in 2025 and stricter quality norms have raised the industry's quality benchmark and eased import pressure
- Offsetting headwind: global steel prices near five-year lows keep imports competitive, and persistent unfair competition and pricing distortions continue to affect parts of the value chain, particularly specialised downstream products
- Core cored wire business regaining ground - volumes grew 14% in FY26 with fourth-quarter volumes rising 32% year-on-year
- Aluminium flipping coils remained subdued amid significant overcapacity and difficult domestic market conditions; the fourth quarter brought an encouraging recovery in volumes and management is prepared to normalise operations as commercial viability improves
- Welding consumables demand from the fabrication and construction sectors remains robust, with the RDSO approval and BIS certification opening doors with major construction and engineering companies and repeat orders rising as the brands gain traction
- The government's fuel blending programme has created a bio-consumables opportunity management estimates at over Rs 1,000 Crore, though significant ethanol industry capacity additions in recent years argue for a measured approach
- Sustainability is becoming a commercial driver - the EU's carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM) is an imminent reality and the Indian steel industry must move towards going green; captive solar has reduced electricity costs by nearly 50% and over 75% of aluminium production uses recycled scrap
- No formal order book is disclosed; management notes that repeat orders in the welding consumables division are rising as the Company's brands gain traction, with more than 10 dealers across more than five states contributing around 90% of the division's sales currently

Distribution capacity has been built out through a dealer-led model spanning more than 10 dealers across more than five states. The newest expansion frontier is biotechnology: a pilot Solid State Fermentation (SSF) R&D facility at Nagpur became operational during the year, with the first fermentation batch commencing in May 2025, focused on enzyme technologies for the ethanol ecosystem; discussions are underway with leading ethanol distilleries and investment has been kept deliberate and capital-disciplined while the segment's long-term potential takes shape. other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Regulatory] UAE's June 2026 ban on aluminium scrap exports, plus similar restrictions in an increasing number of countries, is tightening global scrap availability and raising scrap prices — a direct headwind to the Aluminium Flipping Coils segment, which the company says it is 'monitoring closely.'
- [Sector context] India's BioEconomy crossed an estimated $92 billion in 2022, with a policy/industry target of $150 Bn by 2025 and $300 Bn by 2030 (~17% CAGR) — cited as the backdrop for the company's biotech optionality, not a company-specific figure.
- [Group entity] Bansal Brothers (DB Group) has a separate 11,000 TPA ferroalloys capacity, outside SMLT's own listed entity.
- [Corporate history] Incorporated 1995 (originally an industrial gases unit, sold in 2021); commenced Aluminium Flipping Coils 2002; first in-house Cored Wire mill 2008; started Cored Wire feeder machines 2012; IPO & BSE SME listing 2017; entered Flux Cored Wire business 2018; commenced backward integration into aluminium wire rods for flipping coils 2023; ventured into biotech (bioethanol/biogas, Nagpur) 2024; migrated to/listed on the BSE Main Board since Nov 25, 2021 per the share-price slide.
